answers.answer: ripgrep supplies rg, a cross-platform command-line regex text searcher, normally recursive and respecting ignore rules while skipping hidden and binary files. Shell users and scripts run rg; the repository integration harness also starts the executable. Rust applications can consume the grep library facade. These are evidenced usage surfaces, not a claim to enumerate external adopters.

Principal components: crates/core is the rg application: flags parse/configure execution, haystack adapts directory entries, SearchWorker connects matcher, searcher and printer. grep is the facade. grep-matcher defines the Matcher contract; grep-regex and optional grep-pcre2 implement it. grep-searcher reads/searches haystacks and invokes sinks; grep-printer supplies standard, summary and JSON output. grep-cli supplies I/O, argument conversion and subprocess/decompression helpers. ignore traverses and filters paths; globset matches glob sets. Optional grep-index exposes index construction/discovery; at this pin its CLI read path still delegates to exhaustive ordinary/parallel search.

Rust implementation, organized as a Cargo workspace with TOML manifests, Rust edition 2024 and minimum Rust 1.96. Root package ripgrep owns binary rg (crates/core/main.rs) and explicit integration target tests/tests.rs. Workspace packages live in globset, grep, cli, index, matcher, pcre2, printer, regex, searcher and ignore. Root depends directly on local grep, ignore and optional grep-index; pcre2 and unstable-index are opt-in features. Cargo builds/tests it, with build.rs as the root build script. PCRE2 may link a system library or compile its C source; this is an optional native-library boundary.
Cargo declares rg at crates/core/main.rs. Execution starts at fn main() -> ExitCode, calling run(flags::parse()); flags::parse builds LowArgs then HiArgs. run selects the operational mode.

The application-level sequential loop is fn search(args: &HiArgs, mode: SearchMode) in crates/core/main.rs. Its per-haystack component is SearchWorker::search in crates/core/search.rs; ordinary files dispatch to SearchWorker::search_path and the generic search_path helper. Actual file reading/searching is grep_searcher::Searcher::search_path in crates/searcher/src/searcher/mod.rs.

grep directly depends on grep-cli (../cli), grep-matcher (../matcher), optional grep-pcre2 (../pcre2), grep-printer (../printer), grep-regex (../regex), and grep-searcher (../searcher). Each direction is proved by a dependencies entry in grep/Cargo.toml and its corresponding pub extern crate re-export in grep/src/lib.rs, renamed respectively cli, matcher, pcre2, printer, regex, searcher. PCRE2 is feature-gated in both manifest and code. ignore, globset and grep-index are not direct grep-facade dependencies in this manifest.

Assuming no configuration file adds behavior beyond the stated command: main -> flags::parse -> parse_low (args_os, parser) -> HiArgs::from_low_args -> run. Default mode is Search(Standard), default engine Rust regex. HiArgs identifies the single FILE, chooses one thread, builds the matcher/searcher/standard stdout printer. run selects search because index is off and threads==1. search builds ignore::Walk, adapts entries with HaystackBuilder, and invokes SearchWorker::search for each haystack. The explicit-file haystack gets explicit binary detection; with no stdin, preprocessor or decompressor branch, search_path dispatches RustRegex to generic search_path. It creates the printer's path-aware sink and calls grep_searcher::Searcher::search_path. That opens FILE and calls search_file_maybe_path: a successful mmap goes to search_slice; otherwise ordinary line-mode uses search_reader, decoder and ReadByLine. SliceByLine or ReadByLine runs Core::match_by_line, which selects fast/slow matching, and Core::sink_matched calls the sink. StandardSink::matched updates counts and invokes StandardImpl printing. The resulting sink.has_match becomes SearchResult, then search aggregates it; run ordinarily returns 0 for a match, 1 for none, 2 on errors. Dynamic boundaries: environment/config can alter flags; terminal state affects formatting; mmap availability and transcoding choose the actual reader strategy; pattern/file contents determine regex decisions and matches; OS open/read/write can fail. No concrete output or executed runtime trace was established.

Two direct production call sites are evidenced: sequential search at main.rs calls searcher.search(&haystack), and search_parallel's walker callback calls it on a cloned worker. These callers depend on its Result<SearchResult> and match/statistics behavior. HiArgs::search_worker constructs workers but does not call search. The optional index read wrapper calls search/search_parallel, so it is indirect. Changed matches, errors, output or timing are possible impacts, not established consequences without a specific change and validation. The bounded browser inspection does not prove repository-wide caller exhaustiveness.

tests/misc.rs single_file creates sherlock from SHERLOCK, runs rg Sherlock sherlock and compares the two expected matching lines; line_numbers adds -n. with_heading_default explicitly uses -j1 across ordinary files. rgtest! generates Rust tests, obtains util::setup, and optionally repeats with PCRE2. Dir::command removes RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH and targets rg through CARGO_BIN_EXE_rg or the build-tree fallback; stdout -> output -> raw_output executes Command::output. Thus these are process-level entries into main, not direct calls to SearchWorker. Single-file HiArgs forces threads=1, establishing the sequential path even without -j1. These tests were read, not run.

flags::parse_low first parses process CLI arguments and sets logging. Help/version and --no-config return before configuration loading. Otherwise it calls flags::config::args. That reads std::env::var_os("RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH"); missing or empty values yield no arguments, otherwise the OsString becomes PathBuf. parse opens the file; parse_reader buffers byte lines, trims whitespace, ignores empty lines and # comments, and converts each remaining complete line into one OsString argument (no shell tokenization). Read failure emits a message and returns empty arguments; individual conversion errors are reported alongside accepted arguments. parse_low prepends these config arguments to CLI arguments, reparses a fresh LowArgs, resets logging/message settings, then parse converts to HiArgs. Config therefore enters before high-level execution configuration, not inside SearchWorker.
